s1.syndrome_frame: Palpitations in a pregnant patient with regular narrow QRS tachycardia
salient_findings: Regular cannon waves on jugular venous pulsations
Variable first heart sound on auscultation
key_facts: Patient is a primigravid in their 20s
Palpitations lasted for a few minutes and subsided spontaneously
No associated sweating, syncope, dyspnoea, orthopnoea, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea
Blood pressure was 110/70 mm Hg
Heart rate was 120 beats/min
No chronic medical comorbid conditions
Not taking any medications
Laboratory tests were within normal limits
2-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography showed good biventricular function and normally functioning valves
ECG showed regular narrow QRS tachycardia at a ventricular rate of 103-125 beats/min
